correctness.rationale: The three coefficients are three Frobenius-invariant traces, proved via polynomial expansion and logarithmic derivative. Eight Walsh moments reduce by explicit substitutions to an elliptic Kloosterman sum and a genus-two Artin–Schreier sum. The genus-two zeta numerator follows from H1=0,H2=-2 and Weil reciprocity; Möbius inversion correctly handles even extension degrees by trace annihilation. Uniform Weil bounds prove all-eight positivity from n>=10, and direct exact enumeration resolves n<=9. Standalone checker confirms all eight formula outputs for degrees 2..15 and independently verifies K and H over finite fields 2..10. Finite calculations are only diagnostics, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The claim refines known two-coefficient trace/cotrace counts by an additional formally defined derivative-at-one parity, with an exact eight-class Möbius–Walsh formula, independent genus-two zeta contribution, and a sharp all-eight cutoff. Granger's paper uses a related signature, requiring careful comparison, but the inspected eight-page full text states pair-count identities and bijections, not this three-bit distribution. No equivalent or logically dominating result was found in the checked full text or specific searches; possible alternative-formulation priority risk remains.

Schulz (2023) was only abstract-inspected, so its extended group-action arguments may bear on alternate formulations.

value.rationale: Joint simultaneous prescription at the three canonical rational points infinity, zero and one is a natural refinement of classical trace/cotrace enumeration. Determining all eight counts requires a new genus-two character sum rather than simply two marginal identities; the closed recurrence makes the census uniform for all degrees. The sharp degree-seven threshold is a natural complete attainability boundary, rather than an arbitrary finite table.
